snapped_origin.why: x: -0.1/0.2 = -0.5 floors to -1, div_euclid 8 = -1, times 8 = -8, minus 48 = -56; y: 0.05/0.2 = 0.25 floors to 0, so -48; z: 5.1/0.2 = 25.5 floors to 25, div_euclid 8 = 3, times 8 = 24, minus 48 = -24

x: -1.7/0.4 = -4.25 floors to -5, div_euclid 8 = -1, times 8 = -8, minus 32 = -40; y: 3.3/0.4 = 8.25 floors to 8, div_euclid 8 = 1, times 8 = 8, minus 32 = -24; z: -0.05/0.4 = -0.125 floors to -1, div_euclid 8 = -1, times 8 = -8, minus 32 = -40

choose_rebuild.why: at 0.1 every level wants (floor(0.5) div 8) * 8 - 48 = -48; both levels sit 8 voxels away, so the tie goes to the finest level 0
level 0 already sits on its wanted -48 (offset 0), level 1 wants -48 but sits at -40 (offset 8); the larger offset wins
both levels already sit on their wanted origin, so the maximum offset is 0 and nothing is rebuilt
a null origin counts as offset 0, so both levels are up to date and nothing is rebuilt

rounds.why: new(3) starts clean; mark_stale marks 0,1,2 so the coarsest is 2; complete(2) leaves 0,1; a mark_stale during the round only sets waiting, and start_waiting does nothing while 0,1 are outdated, so the coarsest is 1; once 1 and 0 complete the waiting round is pending; start_waiting then marks all three, so the coarsest is 2 and after all complete nothing waits or is pending

relight.why: the five-level schedule is [0,1,0,2,0,3,0,4]; with no rebuild every call takes the next entry and wraps from 4 back to 0
a fresh cursor takes schedule entry 0, sees it being rebuilt, and takes entry 1 in the same call; the call after advances past 1 to 0

light_schedule.why: the five-level relight order alternates the finest level 0 with each coarser level in turn
four levels use the same alternating order without level 4
three levels use the same alternating order without levels 3 and 4

flood_steps.why: each step halves the previous one from half the 96 grid: 96/2 = 48 then 24, 12, 6, 3, 1
half of the 64 grid is 32, then halving gives 16, 8, 4, 2, 1

flood_pass_count.why: six step lengths, one pass per axis (x, then y, then z), is 6 * 3 = 18 passes, an even count ending in buffer A

volume_bytes.why: R^3 = 884736; 32 * 884736 * 5 = 141557760 for the voxels and 8 * 884736 = 7077888 for seeds, radiance and atlas; the sum is 148635648

forward_lod.why: half a 0.2 m voxel is 0.1 m; scaled errors are 0, 0.08, 0.18, 0.6, so the coarsest level within 0.1 is index 1
half a 0.8 m voxel is 0.4 m; every error is within 0.4, so the coarsest level index 3 wins
an empty chain has no LOD level, so the full mesh index 0 is used
